title: Levelwise truncations of the adic tower
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, $\varpi$ a uniformizer, and $P_n=A/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a scheme, put $B=A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and $R_n=(P_n)_T$, and use the completed-coefficient category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ and strict tower category of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$. Compute its reduction tower $K_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ using one K-flat representative, with level objects $K_n=K\otimes_B^LR_n\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_n))$ and normalization isomorphisms $\rho_n:K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n\simeq K_n$ satisfying the quotient cocycle. Here an adic tower, including the relation between its transitions and normalizations, means [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. All truncations below are the canonical ones [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, def-kun-truncations]. Fix $m\in\mathbf Z$.

(1) Use the following explicit Tor-vanishing hypothesis:
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{R_{n+1}}_p(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),R_n)=0
\quad(n\ge1,\ q\ge m+1,\ p\ge1),\tag{TC}$$
where $\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_p(N,S)=\mathcal H^{-p}(N[0]\otimes_R^LS)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-cohomological-bounds]. Under (TC), the levelwise truncations
$$K_\bullet^-=(\tau^{\le m}K_n)_n,\qquad K_\bullet^+=(\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n)_n$$
are adic towers. Their canonical normalization isomorphisms
$$\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n\simeq\tau^{\le m}K_n,
\qquad \tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n\simeq\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n$$
identify the reduced truncation triangle with the truncation triangle of $K_n$, are natural in maps of reduction towers satisfying (TC), and satisfy the quotient cocycle. A sufficient condition for (TC) is that multiplication by $\varpi$ on $\mathcal H^q(K)$ is injective for every $q\ge m+1$.

Without (TC) the truncated towers need not be adic. For example, if $T$ is nonempty, put $k_T=R_1$ and $K=k_T[-(m+1)]$. Then $\mathcal H^m(K_n)=\mathcal H^{m+1}(K_n)=k_T$ and all other cohomology sheaves vanish, so $\tau^{\le m}K_n\simeq k_T[-m]$. But
$$\mathcal H^{m-p}\bigl((\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n\bigr)\simeq k_T\qquad(p\ge0),$$
which precludes normalization. This assertion concerns cohomology; it does not identify $K_n$ with a split sum in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_n))$.

(2) Suppose in addition that $T$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and that $K_\bullet$ is uniformly bounded constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], with local model complexes having zero terms outside one interval $[d_0,d_1]$. Under (TC), both $K_\bullet^-$ and $K_\bullet^+$ are uniformly bounded constructible in that same sense: each admits a finite stratification and common bounded local complexes of adic-lisse finite-type modules with normalization-compatible reductions. The level cohomology of $K_\bullet^-$ is zero outside $[d_0-1,\min(m,d_1)]$ and that of $K_\bullet^+$ is zero outside $[\max(m+1,d_0-1),d_1]$, with an empty interval meaning zero. This asserts existence of common local models, and does not assert that the original model truncations have finite locally free terms or that a raw mapping cone has no terms below $m+1$.

(3) Without (TC), levelwise truncations are still defined as strict-tower derived objects, and for each $n$ their cohomology is $\mathcal H^i(K_n)$ for $i\le m$ (respectively $i\ge m+1$) and zero in the complementary range. These identifications are natural for the strict transition maps. Under (TC) they are also the identifications obtained from the normalized truncation triangles of (1).

If $K_\bullet$ has compatible etale-origin witnesses, namely $L_n\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},P_n)$ and $\alpha_n:\nu_T^*L_n\simeq K_n$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], with isomorphisms $\beta_n:L_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\simeq L_n$ satisfying the quotient cocycle and $\alpha_n\nu_T^*\beta_n=\rho_n(\alpha_{n+1}\otimes^L R_n)$ under the canonical tensor comparison, then under (TC) the truncated towers have compatible witnesses $\tau^{\le m}L_n$ and $\tau^{\ge m+1}L_n$. Their origin isomorphisms are the truncations of $\alpha_n$ composed with $\nu_T^*\tau\simeq\tau\nu_T^*$, and their normalizations identify the reduced etale truncation triangles with those at level $n$. Here $\nu_T$ is [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and the tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Without (TC), only the levelwise origin isomorphisms and compatibility with strict transition maps are asserted.

proof.text: Apply the levelwise-abelian statement to $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(B)$. Kernels and cokernels in the tower category are the towers of kernels and cokernels. Thus the explicit good truncations, whose only changed term is $\ker d^m$ or $\operatorname{coker}d^m$, evaluate to the good truncations at each level. The same holds before restricting scalars from $R_n$ to $B$, since kernels and cokernels of ring-sheaf modules have their underlying abelian-sheaf kernels and cokernels. The formulas for good-truncation cohomology therefore prove the unconditional cohomology assertions in (3), and functoriality on chain maps gives the truncated strict transitions. These constructions pass to the derived category since the same formulas show that a levelwise quasi-isomorphism stays a levelwise quasi-isomorphism after either truncation. No normalization claim is made in this step. The Lean cohomology clauses use the standard derived-category homology isomorphisms for the truncation counit and unit directly. Exact derived evaluation transports these isomorphisms and the cohomological bounds to each strict-tower level. The scalar-restriction truncation comparisons are characterized by their composites with the counit and unit; their naturality gives both strict semilinear transition squares.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and apply the exact derived scalar extension $F_n=-\otimes^L_{R_{n+1}}R_n$ to the canonical distinguished triangle $X\to K_{n+1}\to Z\to X[1]$, with $X=\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}$ and $Z=\tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}$. Its middle term identifies with $K_n$ by $\rho_n$. Part (a) of the ring-sheaf cohomological-bounds lemma gives $F_nX\in D^{\le m}$. The cohomology of $Z$ is that of $K_{n+1}$ in degrees $q\ge m+1$ and zero below; (TC) is exactly part (b)'s hypothesis at $a=m+1$, so $F_nZ\in D^{\ge m+1}$. All these are assertions in the quotient-coefficient module categories, rather than an identification of those categories with the completed-coefficient category.

proof.text:
Compare the triangle from step 2 with the canonical truncation triangle $X'\to K_n\to Z'\to X'[1]$. Orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(F_nX,Z')=\operatorname{Hom}((F_nX)[1],Z')=0$, since the upper bounds are $m$ and $m-1$ while $Z'\in D^{\ge m+1}$. Triangle-morphism extension supplies a unique comparison with identity middle component. The reverse comparison exists for the same reason; uniqueness makes the two composites identities. Its end components are the required normalization isomorphisms. For a map of input towers, the two resulting comparisons have the same middle component; uniqueness proves naturality. Iterating adjacent reductions, step 2 gives the same end bounds at each stage. The direct and iterated comparisons then have the same middle component by the original quotient cocycle, so uniqueness proves the end-component cocycles.

Apply the scalar-extension-unit triangle lemma to $R_{n+1}\to R_n$ and restrict to $B$. Compose its triangle morphism with the comparison above. Its middle component is the original strict transition by the definition of an adic tower. Restriction is exact and preserves cohomological bounds. Thus in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$, $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Z')=\operatorname{Hom}(X[1],Z')=0$. Triangle-morphism extension makes the end components with this middle component unique. The functorial truncations of the original strict transition from step 1 give another such comparison, so their end maps equal these composites. This proves strict-transition compatibility and the normalized cohomology assertion of (3). For the standalone transition-compatibility clause, no additional unit-triangle construction is necessary: the first two commutative squares of the supplied normalized triangle comparison suffice. Take their adjuncts using naturality of the scalar-adjunction unit. For the lower comparison, compose with the exact-restriction truncation isomorphism and use the universal property of the truncation counit. For the upper comparison, precompose with the truncation unit and use its universal property; exact restriction preserves the required lower bound. Transport across the stored level equalities. The standalone naturality clause follows by applying the standard t-structure triangle-map uniqueness theorem to the two triangle morphisms with the given common middle component. K2 implementation: scalar_truncation_triangle applies the published tensor cohomological bounds and the standard t-structure triangle isomorphism and uniqueness APIs. construct_truncations builds the actual lower and upper towers. The adjunct of each endpoint isomorphism is characterized by its composite with the truncation counit or unit; this identifies it with the truncated original semilinear transition. Truncation naturality and the scalar-restriction composition comparison then give all-pair quotient cocycles and the strict evaluation transition equations.

proof.text: For the sufficient condition, the finite free $A$-resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi^a}A]\to P_a$, after the completed constant-sheaf base change, gives $[B\xrightarrow{\varpi^a}B]\to R_a$ for every $a\ge1$. In particular $\varpi^a$ is injective on $B$ and $R_a=B/\varpi^aB$. Tensoring gives the multiplication triangle $K\xrightarrow{\varpi^a}K\to K_a\to K[1]$. Its long exact cohomology sequence yields $0\to\mathcal H^q(K)/\varpi^a\to\mathcal H^q(K_a)\to\mathcal H^{q+1}(K)[\varpi^a]\to0$. Under the sufficient condition the last term is zero for $q\ge m+1$, so $\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1})=M/\varpi^{n+1}M$, where $M=\mathcal H^q(K)$ has injective $\varpi$ action. The free resolution of $R_n$ over $R_{n+1}$ has differentials, starting just before its degree-zero term, $\varpi^n,\varpi,\varpi^n,\varpi,\ldots$. It is exact because $\ker(\varpi^n:R_{n+1}\to R_{n+1})=\varpi R_{n+1}$ and $\ker(\varpi)=\varpi^nR_{n+1}$. It is K-flat by the bounded-above flat-complex lemma. Tensoring it with $M/\varpi^{n+1}M$ is exact in all negative degrees: injectivity of $\varpi$ on $M$ gives respectively $\ker\varpi^n=\varpi M/\varpi^{n+1}M$ and $\ker\varpi=\varpi^nM/\varpi^{n+1}M$. These sheaf equalities can be checked after local lifts along the quotient epimorphism. This computes every higher Tor as zero and proves (TC), without a spectral-sequence convergence assertion or a claim that $B$ is itself a discrete valuation ring.

proof.text: Assume $T$ is nonempty and take $K=k_T[-(m+1)]$. The same two-term $B$-resolution of $R_n$ gives $K_n$ as $[k_T\xrightarrow{0}k_T][-(m+1)]$ after restricting scalars to $B$. Thus its two nonzero cohomology sheaves are $k_T$ in degrees $m,m+1$. The lower truncation has just one nonzero cohomology sheaf and is therefore $k_T[-m]$ in $D(R_n)$. Compute its next reduction using the periodic free $R_{n+1}$-resolution of $R_n$ from step 4: after tensoring with $k_T$ every differential is zero. Thus $\mathcal H^{m-p}=k_T$ for every $p\ge0$. Here $k_T$ is nonzero: the constant coefficient sections $0$ and $1$ on $T$ remain distinct after every pro-etale covering, since a covering of a nonempty scheme has a nonempty member. Thus the negative-degree cohomology just computed cannot equal that of $k_T[-m]$. On the empty scheme all these sheaves are zero, so this example does not obstruct normalization. The computation does not split the original two-degree object in $D(R_n)$; the two-term $B$-resolution was used only to compute its cohomology. This proves the counterexample and, independently, shows why freeness of terms alone cannot justify (TC).

source.place: Statement (1), torsion counterexample; corrected to assert cohomology rather than an R_n-linear splitting; nonemptiness is necessary for the nonzero coefficient-sheaf counterexample

proof.text: Assume the hypotheses of (2). On a local model domain $U\to T$, let $B_U$ denote the inverse image of $B$, without identifying it with the completed coefficient sheaf formed anew on $U$. The exact pro-etale inverse image, with coefficient ring its own inverse image, pulls the resolution $[B\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B]\to R_n$ back to $[B_U\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}B_U]\to R_n|_U$. This is a bounded free, hence K-flat, resolution. Tensoring a model $L$ with zero terms outside $[d_0,d_1]$ therefore represents its derived reduction by a complex with zero terms outside $[d_0-1,d_1]$. The same is true of $K_n|_U$ by the model isomorphisms. Restriction to strata and their coverings is exact. Each original level cohomology sheaf is intrinsically constructible: this follows directly from its finite lisse local restrictions on the given finite stratification. By finite-ring constructible-sheaf comparison it is the pullback of an etale constructible sheaf. Local vanishing implies vanishing on its stratum by the sheaf condition for the covering. The pro-etale inverse-image stalk comparison identifies the stalk on a stratum with the original stalk at the image geometric point. Every geometric point of T factors through its unique stratum. The etale/pro-etale comparison-stalk isomorphism therefore makes every geometric stalk of the etale origin zero. Conservativity of the etale geometric points implies that this origin, and hence the original cohomology sheaf, is zero. Thus the original levels, and hence both truncated levels, have a common finite cohomological interval. The sharper intervals displayed in (2) follow by intersecting $[d_0-1,d_1]$ with the surviving truncation range.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), the pulled-back two-term quotient resolution; blueprint Proof Step 2, amplitude bookkeeping, with the possible Tor degree d_0-1 retained

proof.text: The original local model reductions have finite lisse cohomology on the common strata. At each level, truncation only retains these cohomology sheaves or replaces them by zero, so each truncated level has intrinsically constructible cohomology, with the same finite stratification, as required in the normalized local-effectivity statement. Step 6 supplies a uniform finite cohomological interval. Steps 2-3 supply the quotient-coefficient level objects and normalized derived reductions inducing the strict transitions and satisfying the cocycle. Finally $T$ is Noetherian by the explicit hypothesis of (2). All hypotheses of normalized constructible local effectivity now hold, separately for $K_\bullet^-$ and $K_\bullet^+$. Its conclusion is exactly the common finite stratification, bounded adic-lisse finite-type local models, and compatible reduction identifications required in (2). It makes no assertion about the terms of the particular raw truncation or raw cone of the original models, which is why the false free-term clause is not used.

proof.text:
Under (TC), the etale upper cohomology sheaves are also $P_n$-acyclic for reduction from $P_{n+1}$. Indeed the derived tensor comparison for the ringed comparison morphism identifies the pullback of each of their higher Tor sheaves with $\operatorname{Tor}^{R_{n+1}}_p(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),R_n)$, using step 8's cohomology comparison and $\alpha_{n+1}$. This is zero by (TC). The sheaf comparison unit is an isomorphism, so $
u_T^*F=0$ implies $F=
u_{T,*}
u_T^*F=0$; hence the etale Tor sheaves vanish. Apply steps 2-3 in the etale module categories to $ eta_n$ to obtain normalization isomorphisms of the truncated etale levels and their cocycles. Pulling the resulting comparison of truncation triangles to the pro-etale site and composing with the truncated $\alpha_n$ gives a comparison whose middle map is $\alpha_n
u_T^* eta_n=ho_n(\alpha_{n+1}\otimes^LR_n)$ by the original compatibility assumption. Step 3's uniqueness therefore gives precisely the two truncated normalization-compatibility equations, not just levelwise origin isomorphisms. The tensor comparisons used here come from the natural balancing map on K-flat representatives: $(x\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes q(b)a$. For three quotients either composition sends a pure tensor to the same product, so the same identifications respect quotient composition. This completes (3).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q10-dda730325 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all nine steps of the item and the new node in full against the current main-20261015 blueprint proof, Stacks 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change, checked in tags/tags), the unit sk-rem-rest (no steps, so there is no route departure) and every cited node statement. The new step-3 argument is correct. lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-unit-triangles turns the unit eta into a morphism of triangles Delta -> UF(Delta) for R_{n+1} -> R_n. After restriction along pi_{n+1}, its middle map Res(rho_n)∘eta is the strict transition, by the definition in def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower. In D(B), X is in D^{<=m}, X[1] in D^{<=m-1} and Z' in D^{>=m+1}, so lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension(2) gives uniqueness of the end maps. The new node is true: it is the derived unit x -> x⊗1 on K-flat complexes, with i_{P[1]}=i_P[1], and the connecting square chi_X UF(w) eta_Z = eta_X[1] w follows from naturality plus the shift equation. I tested it on R=S, on S=0 and on Z -> Z/2. It mentions no tower, TC or witnesses, so it does not restate the parent (D1/D2 pass). It is not a duplicate: lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction covers only O_E-hat -> A_{E,n} and has no triangle clause, and lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-triangle-morphism assumes the shift-compatible transformation that the new node supplies. The other steps check out. Step 2: bounds lemma (b) at a=m+1 has exactly TC as its hypothesis. Step 3, first paragraph: Hom(F_nX,Z') and Hom(F_nX[1],Z') vanish. blueprint_update.statement:
Let the adic datum be $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, with $P_n=A_{E,n}$,
and let $K_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ be an adic tower (an
object with normalization isomorphisms
$K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$ satisfying the quotient
cocycle), given by a K-flat representative $QK$ of a single object $K$ of
the underlying pro-etale complex category, $K_n=QK\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$.
Then for every $m\in\mathbf Z$:

1. the levelwise truncations
   $$
    \tau^{\le m}K_\bullet:=(\tau^{\le m}K_n)_n,\qquad
    \tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet:=(\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n)_n,
   $$
   of the levelwise t-structure of $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ (whose
   evaluations are the levelwise canonical truncations of the strict-tower
   representatives) are adic towers, with canonical normalization
   isomorphisms
   $$
    \tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
    \xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\le m}K_n,\qquad
    \tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
    \xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n
   $$
   satisfying the quotient cocycle, *provided* the following
   Tor-compatibility condition (1) holds: for every $n$ and every $q\ge m+1$
   the canonical morphism
   $$
    \mathcal H^q(K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
    \longrightarrow\mathcal H^q(K_n)
   $$
   is an isomorphism;
2. if $K_\bullet$ is uniformly bounded constructible, with local models
   $L_{\alpha j}$ supported in $[d_0,d_1]$ and with the isomorphisms
   $K_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}\simeq L_{\alpha j}\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ for every
   $n$, then $\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet$ is uniformly bounded constructible with
   the local models $\tau^{\le m}L_{\alpha j}$ (supported in
   $[\min(d_0,m),m]$), and $\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet$ is uniformly bounded
   constructible with the local models
   $$
    C_{\alpha j}:=\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(\tau^{\le m}L_{\alpha j}
    \longrightarrow L_{\alpha j}\bigr)
   $$
   (supported in $[m+1,d_1]$), the terms of both families of models being
   finite locally free and their reductions having finite lisse cohomology;
3. for every $n$ there are canonical isomorphisms
   $$
    \mathcal H^i\bigl((\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet)_n\bigr)
     \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^i(K_n)\quad(i\le m),
    \qquad
    \mathcal H^i\bigl((\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet)_n\bigr)=0\quad(i>m),
   $$
   and analogously
   $$
    \mathcal H^i\bigl((\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet)_n\bigr)
     \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^i(K_n)\quad(i\ge m+1),
    \qquad
    \mathcal H^i\bigl((\tau^{\ge m+1}K_\bullet)_n\bigr)=0\quad(i\le m),
   $$
   compatible with the normalization maps; if the tower carries compatible
   etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]
   $(L_n^{\mathrm{et}},\alpha_n)$, the truncated towers carry the
   compatible witnesses
   $(\tau^{\le m}L_n^{\mathrm{et}},\nu^*\tau^{\le m}\circ\alpha_n)$ and
   $(\tau^{\ge m+1}L_n^{\mathrm{et}},\nu^*\tau^{\ge m+1}\circ\alpha_n)$.

Statements (i) and (ii) are asserted under the Tor-compatibility
condition (1); statement (iii) holds unconditionally, being a formal
property of the canonical truncations.

Since $\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n$ has cohomology
$\operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),P_n)$ in degree $-p$,
condition (1) says that for $q\ge m+1$ the higher Tor terms
$\operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),P_n)$, $p\ge1$, vanish
and $\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1})\otimes_{P_{n+1}}P_n\to\mathcal H^q(K_n)$ is an
isomorphism; these Tor terms are the Künneth obstruction in the spectral
sequence
$$
 E_2^{p,q}=\operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}
 \bigl(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),P_n\bigr)\Rightarrow
 \mathcal H^{q-p}(K_n)
$$
of the reduction morphism. A sufficient condition is that the cohomology
sheaves $\mathcal H^i(K)$ of the ambient object (equivalently, of the local
models) be $\varpi$-torsion-free (over the discrete valuation ring $A_T$
equivalently flat) for all $i\ge m+1$, because then
$\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1})=\mathcal H^q(K)\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_{n+1})_T$ has no
higher $\varpi$-torsion and the morphism of (1) is the identity on
$(\mathcal H^q(K)/\varpi^{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n$.

*In general the levelwise truncations are not adic towers*: the failure
is exactly the Tor-contribution. For instance, for
$K=(A_T/\varpi)[-(m+1)]$ (a single shift of the constant
$\varpi$-torsion sheaf) one has
$$
 K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T
 =\bigl((A_T/\varpi)\oplus(A_T/\varpi)[1]\bigr)[-(m+1)]
$$
for every $n\ge1$ — the two-term Koszul resolution of $(P_n)_T$ over
$A_T$ gives
$\operatorname{Tor}_1^{A_T}(A_T/\varpi,(P_n)_T)=A_T/\varpi$ — and hence
$\tau^{\le m}K_n=(A_T/\varpi)[-m]$ for every $n$, whereas
$$
 (\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
 =\bigl((A_T/\varpi)\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\bigr)[-m],
$$
whose cohomology is $A_T/\varpi$ in *every* degree $\le m$ (since
$\operatorname{Tor}_i^{P_{n+1}}(A_T/\varpi,P_n)=A_T/\varpi$ for all
$i\ge0$, $n\ge1$); this is not $(A_T/\varpi)[-m]$, so the levelwise
truncated tower $\tau^{\le m}K_\bullet$ fails to be an adic tower.

*Local freeness of the terms of a model does not imply (1)*: for the
two-term complex $P_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\ \varpi\ }P_{n+1}$ the terms are
free while the first cohomology is the torsion module $P_n$, so freeness of
the terms forces neither torsion-freeness of the cohomology nor the
vanishing of the higher Tor terms in (1). Flatness of the cohomology
sheaves of the local models is strictly stronger than finiteness of their
terms.

proof.text:
The evaluations $\operatorname{ev}_n$ are exact and jointly conservative, so
the levelwise t-structure of $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ has the levelwise
canonical truncations of the statement, computed on the strict-tower
representatives.

*Step 1: the normalization isomorphisms of (i).* The derived tensor functor
$-\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n$ is triangulated, being the left derived functor of
$-\otimes_{P_{n+1}}P_n$ (take a K-flat resolution of $P_n$); tensoring the
truncation triangle of $K_{n+1}$,
$$
 \tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}\longrightarrow K_{n+1}
 \longrightarrow\tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}\longrightarrow
 \tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}[1],
$$
with $P_n$ and using the normalization
$K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\simeq K_n$ gives the triangle
$$
 (\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
 \longrightarrow K_n
 \longrightarrow(\tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1})\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n
 \longrightarrow .
$$
Künneth spectral sequence. For a complex $M$ of $P_{n+1}$-modules there is
the Künneth spectral sequence of the derived tensor
$$
 E_2^{p,q}=\operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}\bigl(\mathcal H^q(M),P_n\bigr)
 \Rightarrow\mathcal H^{q-p}\bigl(M\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\bigr).
$$
For $M=\tau^{\le m}K_{n+1}$ one has $\mathcal H^q(M)=0$ for $q>m$, so all
the $E_2$-terms of total degree $>m$ vanish and the first end term of the
triangle has no cohomology above degree $m$. For $M=\tau^{\ge m+1}K_{n+1}$,
the $E_2$-terms of total degree $\le m$ are exactly the higher Tor-terms
$$
 \operatorname{Tor}_p^{P_{n+1}}\bigl(\mathcal H^q(K_{n+1}),P_n\bigr),
 \qquad q\ge m+1,\ p\ge q-m\ge1,
$$
of the cohomology sheaves of degree $\ge m+1$; by the same spectral sequence
applied to $K_{n+1}$, the Tor-compatibility condition (1) of the statement —
whose displayed morphisms are the $p=0$ edge terms in degrees $q\ge m+1$ —
is exactly the vanishing of all these higher Tor-terms (a sufficient
condition being the $\varpi$-torsion-freeness, i.e. flatness over the
discrete valuation ring $A_T$, of the cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^i(K)$
of the ambient object for $i\ge m+1$, as in the statement; for the towers of
the form $K_n=QK\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ the cohomology sheaves of the models
are then flat over the respective $P_n$ by base change along $A_T\to P_n$).
Under (1) the second end term therefore has no cohomology in degrees $\le m$,
and the triangle above is a truncation triangle of $K_n$; truncation
triangles are unique (a triangle whose end terms, endowed with the displayed
maps, lie in the full subcategories of complexes with cohomology in $\le m$
and $\ge m+1$ respectively is canonically isomorphic to the canonical
truncation triangle of the middle term), so the canonical normalization
isomorphisms of (i) follow, and the cocycle is inherited from the quotient
cocycle of $K_\bullet$. When condition (1) fails, the displayed end terms of
the triangle carry the Tor-contributions of the Künneth spectral sequence in
the wrong degrees, and the composite is in general only a canonical
morphism, not an isomorphism; the counterexample after the statement shows the
failure is real.

*Step 2: the models of (ii).* The local models here are those of the
bounded constructible tower. (Under the Tor-compatibility condition (1),
which the hypotheses of (ii) ensure throughout: the cohomology sheaves of
the local models are the ones of the ambient object.) The terms of
$\tau^{\le m}L_{\alpha j}$ are $L_{\alpha j}^i$ for $i<m$, and $\ker(d^m)$
in degree $m$: after refining the pro-etale covering so that each
$U_{\alpha j}$ is connected, $A_T|_{U_{\alpha j}}$ is the constant completed
valuation ring, over which submodules of finite free modules are finite
free, so the terms are finite locally free. The support and the finite lisse
reduction cohomology of the models follow from the isomorphisms of (iii)
(the reductions of the truncated models have the same cohomology sheaves as
the reductions of $L_{\alpha j}$ in the surviving degrees, by Step 1 applied
locally). The terms of $C_{\alpha j}$ are direct sums of terms of
$L_{\alpha j}$ and of $\tau^{\le m}L_{\alpha j}$, hence finite locally free;
its support is $[m+1,d_1]$, and, being the cone of the model truncation map,
its reductions are constant by the same local computation, since
$$
 C_{\alpha j}\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T
 \cong\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(
   \tau^{\le m}K_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}\longrightarrow K_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}\bigr)
 \cong\tau^{\ge m+1}K_n|_{U_{\alpha j}}.
$$
The intertwinings with the quotient transition maps are the local forms of
the canonical isomorphisms of (i).

*Step 3: the cohomology isomorphisms and the witnesses of (iii).* The
formulas of (iii) hold by construction of the levelwise truncations of the
strict-tower representatives. Under condition (1), for $i\le m$ the triangle
of Step 1 has end terms with zero cohomology in the relevant degrees, so the
long exact cohomology sequence of the tensored truncation triangle yields
the displayed isomorphisms of (iii) directly (compatible with the
normalization maps of (i) by their canonicality); the etale-origin witnesses
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] are transported by the exactness of the
site-comparison inverse image $\nu^*$
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]: for a witness
$K_n\simeq\nu^*L_n^{\mathrm{et}}$ one has
$\tau^{\le m}K_n\simeq\nu^*\tau^{\le m}L_n^{\mathrm{et}}$, and the
normalization compatibility is the naturality of $\nu^*$.
